text:
Predicates:
InCity(x) ::: x is a city.
InState(x, y) ::: x is in state y.
CityIn(x, y) ::: x is a city in y.
State(y) ::: y is a state.
InSameState(x, y) ::: x and y are in the same state.

Premises:
CityIn(butte, montana) ∧ CityIn(helena, montana) ∧ CityIn(missoula, montana) ::: The cities of Butte, Helena, and Missoula are in Montana.
∃x (CityIn(x, montana) ∧ CityIn(whiteSulphurSprings, montana)) ::: White Sulphur Springs and Butte are cities in Montana.
¬InState(stPierre, montana) ::: St Pierre is not in Montana.
∀x (CityIn(x, butte) → ¬InState(x, stPierre)) ::: Any city in Butte is not in St Pierre.
∀x, y (CityIn(x, y) ∧ CityIn(z, y) → x = z) ::: A city can only be in one state (except for specified cities).

Conclusion:
InSameState(stPierre, bismarck) ::: St Pierre and Bismarck are in the same state.
